text: Beds it is. What you’ve described lines up closely with a hospital we worked with.
Let me show you their day rather than describe it. One thing to watch: that bed stopped earning hours before it was empty.
Does that look like your day? Is there anything about your own setup you’d add?
chat.note: The bed stops earning long before it is empty.
prompts: Yes, that looks like our day

blocks.title: The bed that stopped earning
blocks.deck: One bed through one day. Watch where the bill stops, and how long it stays stopped.

stops.title: Final bill closed
stops.detail: The leaving patient’s final bill is closed and sent for insurance approval. The patient is still in the bed.
stops.bill: The bill stops here. Nothing more is charged to this bed.

stops.title: Approval, payment, family briefing
stops.line: The patient is still in the bed.
stops.detail: Approval comes through, the family pays and is told what happens at home. All this time the patient is still in the bed.
stops.bill: Still nothing billing, with the bed still in use.

stops.title: Patient leaves, bed made ready
stops.detail: The patient finally leaves. Housekeeping cleans the bed and gets it ready for the next patient.
stops.bill: The bed is empty now. Still nothing billing.

stops.title: Next patient admitted
stops.line: Only now does a new bill open.
stops.detail: The next patient is admitted. Only now does a new bill open against this bed.

blocks.caption: Nothing bills on this bed across this whole stretch. That includes pharmacy, tests, scans and procedures.

blocks.label: Dead bed time
blocks.value: Last bill closed to next bill opened
blocks.sub: Often half a day or more on one bed. Most hospitals have never measured it on its own.
